concepts.title: Surface Area of a Combination of Solids
concepts.definition: Solids around us combine basic shapes - a capsule is a cylinder with two hemispheres, a tent is a cone on a cylinder; the surface area of such a combination is found by adding the visible curved surfaces of the parts and dropping the faces hidden at the joints.
concepts.key_idea: Add only what shows: hidden joining faces leave the surface total.
concepts.textbook_ref: jemh112.txt section 12.2 (surface area of a combination of solids)

concepts.title: Volume of a Combination of Solids
concepts.definition: The volume of a combined solid is simply the sum of the volumes of its parts: cylinder, cone and hemisphere each contribute their own measure - pi r squared h for the cylinder, one-third of it for a cone of the same base, and two-thirds pi r cubed for a hemisphere.
concepts.key_idea: Volumes add: parts that join fill space without overlapping.
concepts.textbook_ref: jemh112.txt section 12.3 (volume of a combination of solids)

concepts.title: Conversion of Solids from One Shape to Another
concepts.definition: Melting or recasting a solid changes its shape but not its volume: a sphere melted into a wire, or dough rolled from a cone, keeps the same volume - equating the volumes before and after finds the new dimensions.
concepts.key_idea: Volume is the invariant: equate before and after to find the new dimensions.
